summary: TalkSport's Michael Benson ranks the ten craziest fight endings in boxing history, from Floyd Mayweather's KO of Victor Ortiz to Mike Tyson biting Evander Holyfield's ear. The list includes referee mishaps, interference from managers, parents and a TV camera, and fighters who simply walked out or broke down. Ordinary bad decisions and Tyson Fury singing are excluded.
one_line: TalkSport ranks boxing's ten wildest fight endings, with Tyson's 1997 ear bite against Holyfield at number one.
key_facts: Floyd Mayweather knocked out Victor Ortiz in 2011 with two hooks after Ortiz headbutted him, was docked a point, and tried to hug him; Mayweather's pro career lasted 50 bouts.
HBO analyst Larry Merchant, aged 80, argued with Mayweather after the Ortiz fight and said he wanted to kick Floyd's ass.

Ricky Hatton's elbow cut Stephen Smith in Hatton's 30th fight; Smith's father and cornerman Darkie entered the ring and shoved referee Mickey Vann, causing a disqualification in front of 15,000 fans in Manchester.

In 1998 referee Mills Lane sent Bernard Hopkins through the ropes while separating a clinch with Robert Allen; Hopkins claimed injury, and in the rematch a year later he knocked Allen out in round seven.
Efe Ajagba, then 5-0, won in the first second of round one in 2018 when Curtis Harper left the ring at the opening bell over a contract situation, giving Ajagba an official KO1, 0:01.
In 1991 Elijah Tillery was disqualified against Riddick Bowe after kicking him; Bowe's manager Rock Newman hauled Tillery out of the ring with a neckbreaker.
Kermit Cintron dived through the ropes into a table in round four of his 2004 fight with Paul Williams, left on a stretcher in a neck brace, and Williams won on the scorecards.

Adolpho Washington's 1993 challenge to Virgil Hill for the 175lb title ended when his swollen eye hit a TV camera as he sat down after round 11, causing a cut; Hill was declared technical decision winner.

In their 1997 rematch Oliver McCall cried, wandered the ring and stopped punching against Lennox Lewis, and Mills Lane waved the fight off; McCall had been arrested for throwing a Christmas tree across a hotel lobby in the buildup.

In 1989 Tony Wilson's 62-year-old mother hit Steve McCarthy with her shoe after McCarthy scored a third-round knockdown; McCarthy refused to continue, citing a head wound needing stitches, and Wilson was declared the winner.
In the 1997 rematch Mike Tyson bit Evander Holyfield's ear, was allowed to continue, then bit the other ear and was thrown out; Tyson was fined $3 million and banned for 15 months.
Tyson and Holyfield later made up and remain firm friends.
